connection_condition: The identifier column of the patient table carries the identity of the patient row.
description: A patient record is identified by its patient identifier; the identifier is a component of the patient record and has no meaning without it.

connection_condition: The identifier column of the laboratory table corresponds to the identifier column of the patient table.
description: A patient is composed of the laboratory measurements taken for that patient; a laboratory panel cannot exist without the patient it belongs to. Every laboratory identifier resolves to a patient record.

connection_condition: The identifier column of the examination table corresponds to the identifier column of the patient table, but the overlap between the two identifier sets is small.
description: An examination belongs to a patient, yet the identifier linkage is sparsely populated: only a small minority of examination identifiers resolve to a patient record, so examination-based cohorts and patient demographics cannot generally be combined.
Age is derived per patient from the birthday by subtracting the year of birth from the year of the reference date; no age value is stored.

Every laboratory result is interpreted against the reference interval of its own analyte, so a result and a reference interval are always considered together even though no column stores the interval.
The abnormal status of a laboratory result is derived by comparing the measured value with the reference interval of its analyte.
The positive coagulation status of an examination is derived from the three panel assays: it holds when any one of them records a positive code.

connection_condition: Recorded symptoms are present on exactly those examinations whose thrombosis grade is greater than zero.
description: Recorded symptoms and the thrombosis grade describe the same clinical event from two angles: a narrative of the event and an ordinal severity, and their presence patterns coincide exactly in the observed data.

connection_condition: Both values are recorded on the same examination record, but neither is derivable from the other.
description: The antinuclear antibody titre and the antinuclear antibody pattern are companion findings on one examination; they are recorded side by side yet carry independent values, including records where one is populated and the other is blank.

connection_condition: Both columns hold the date of a data-collection encounter for a patient and share the same date value domain, but they live in different tables.
description: The laboratory test date and the examination date both express the date on which a patient encounter produced data. A date window applied to a laboratory-defined cohort uses the laboratory date, while a window applied to an examination-defined cohort uses the examination date.
Systemic lupus erythematosus is one of the disease designations that can appear in the diagnosis field.
Sjogren's syndrome is one of the disease designations that can appear in the diagnosis field.
The two diseases frequently appear as co-listed designations inside a single diagnosis string, so selecting patients for one of them also captures patients who carry both.

connection_condition: The antibody level and the thrombosis grade are recorded on the same examination record.
description: Anti-cardiolipin antibody of the IgM isotype is an antiphospholipid marker assessed alongside the degree of thrombosis recorded for the same examination.
